faqs.q: What is a 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector used for?
faqs.a: A cement dust collector captures cement dust at a cement handling site. This low-capex, low-OPEX unit drops the air velocity at the inlet, lets the dust separate by gravity inside a 50 cu.ft. vessel, and collects it in a synthetic fabric bag on the dump line.

faqs.q: What vessel sizes does the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector come in?
faqs.a: The vessel volume is adjustable on a project basis, with 25 to 200 cu.ft. envelopes as standard. This listing is the 50 cu.ft. size. State the dust-generating throughput and the venting airflow on the RFQ to choose the vessel.

faqs.q: How does the velocity-drop principle in the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector work?
faqs.a: Cement dust is captured by a drop in velocity at the inlet and by gravity separation inside the vessel. The collected material falls into a synthetic fabric bag attached to the dump line with quick-release clamps, so the bag is changed without tools.

faqs.q: What is the collection bag in the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector made of?
faqs.a: The collection bag is a synthetic fabric bag on the dump line, held with quick-release clamps. Send the vessel material and coating requirement on the RFQ if the site is offshore or corrosive.

faqs.q: What monitoring options does the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector offer?
faqs.a: An optional differential pressure indicator and a remote alarm are available, which show when the bag is loading up. State on the RFQ whether remote alarm signals are needed in the control cabin.

faqs.q: What does the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector connect to?
faqs.a: It connects to the vent lines of cement silos, the cutting bottle and the mixing system. See [cement silos](/c/cementing-silos), [cutting bottles](/c/cementing-cutting-bottle) and [cementing units](/c/cementing-units) for the equipment it serves.

faqs.q: How does the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector differ from a rock catcher?
faqs.a: A dust collector cleans the air leaving the cement system, while a [rock catcher](/p/cement-rock-catcher-inline-vessel-ss-screen-selectable-mesh) is an inline screen that stops debris and cement lumps in the transfer line. Both protect the system, in different places.

faqs.q: Where is the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector used?
faqs.a: It is used at cement handling sites where dust must be controlled and capex and operating cost are limited, including cementing unit charge points and silo vents.

faqs.q: How often should the cement dust collector bag be emptied?
faqs.a: Empty the bag when the differential pressure indicator rises or the remote alarm sounds, and inspect the fabric for wear at each change. The quick-release clamps make the bag change simple.

faqs.q: What should I send for a cement dust collector quotation?
faqs.a: Send the airflow or silo size being vented, the vessel size you expect, the alarm and indicator options, and the mounting. See the [guide to cementing and drilling-fluid equipment](/blog/cementing-and-drilling-fluid-equipment) for how the equipment connects.

faqs.q: Can the vessel size of the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector be changed?
faqs.a: Yes. The vessel volume is adjustable on a project basis from 25 to 200 cu.ft., so the 50 cu.ft. unit can be resized to the site throughput. Send the vent airflow so the right size is quoted.

faqs.q: Does Indus stock the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector?
faqs.a: Yes. We list the 50 cu.ft. velocity-drop cement dust collector as ex-stock from our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send your capacity, drive and mounting requirements through [our contact page](/contact) for a quotation.
